Yesterday, the House Appropriations Committee debated the Fiscal Year 2027 Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies funding bill. While it did a good job supporting Army Corps of Engineers projects which help many communities with vital waterways and flood mitigation, its shortcomings outweigh its positive elements.

It cuts programs that help us diversify our energy supply chain and make sure that America stays on the cutting edge of research and development, it undermines nuclear security, and it abandons communities dealing with nuclear contamination from past defense projects. As a result, American families and businesses are going to face higher fuel and utility costs and many communities will be left less safe.

During the debate, I tried to improve the bill by supporting an amendment that would increase the critical minerals and energy innovation fund and restore the electricity account. This would help make America more energy independent, maintain the electrical grid and help make sure it is reliable, and ensure that we are not relying on foreign adversaries for materials vital to manufacturing and technology that drive our economy.

The amendment would help make sure that American families can afford to keep the lights on, farmers can operate, and local businesses can continue to function.

Colorado's growth depends on reliable, affordable energy.

Right now, communities across Northern Colorado are facing a simple reality: we don't have enough power generation to keep up with growing demand. That means fewer jobs, fewer homes, and fewer opportunities for Colorado families.

That's why I'm leading efforts to cut red tape and streamline the permitting process through legislation like the FIRE Act,  CERTAIN Act, and the SPEED Act. We need an all-of-the-above energy strategy that allows us to build critical infrastructure faster, strengthen our electric grid, and keep energy affordable and reliable.

If we want to support growth, attract businesses, and lower costs for hardworking Coloradans, we have to start building again.

This investment will pave nearly two miles of roadway, improve drainage, enhance safety, and help keep Northern Colorado moving as our region continues to grow.

I secured $3.5 million to help expand the Greeley-Weld County Airport, and I’m continuing to fight for additional funding to support a new air traffic control tower and future growth.

As Northern Colorado continues to grow, investments like these will improve safety, create jobs, attract new businesses, strengthen our economy, and help relieve air traffic congestion and noise over the Denver metro area for generations to come.

Before I was sworn into Congress, I promised to reopen the Tyrone Post Office, which had previously suffered extensive structural damage due to a fire.  As of today, the Tyrone Post Office is fully open for business.

During a Congressional oversight hearing, I asked the Postmaster General to accelerate the Post Office’s reconstruction, which had been delayed for years.  He and his team swiftly reacted, and worked closely with my team to achieve this goal.

Thank you to Tyrone Mayor Eric Dial and the Tyrone Town Council for your partnership and forceful advocacy, and thank you to Postmaster General David Steiner, and Kayla Dufrene, Brandy Jackson, and Sharon Alston of the Postal Service for your leadership on this important project.

As we reflect this week on the costly sacrifices made to defend our freedom, we are inspired by these young men and women preparing to attend the United States Military Academy at West Point, the United States Naval Academy at Annapolis, and the United States Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs.

May the stories of these heroes continue to inspire us and the next generation of guardians of our freedom.

May their sacrifices and the heartbreak felt by their families remind us of the cost of freedom and the price of liberty on this solemn day of remembrance.

Our office was honored to attend the American Red Cross Open House and recognize the incredible work the organization performs in communities across the nation and here in the CNMI. 

We are especially grateful to the NMI Chapter of the Red Cross for their partnership and dedication following Super Typhoon Sinlaku, providing shelter, assistance, and preparedness efforts that have helped our islands recover and rebuild. 

Their commitment to serving others continues to make a meaningful difference throughout the Commonwealth.

Our office is pleased to share that the Commonwealth Ports Authority has been awarded $2.095 million through the FAA’s Airport Terminal Program to support improvements at Saipan International Airport. 

This investment will modernize terminal operations, improve flexibility for airlines, and help reduce wait times for passengers traveling through the CNMI.

Congratulations to Team CPA on securing this important funding. Strengthening our airport infrastructure helps improve connectivity, supports economic growth, and enhances the travel experience for residents and visitors alike.

Our office welcomes the Environmental Protection Agency’s announcement of more than $15 million in federal funding to help address PFAS contamination, replace aging lead water pipes, and strengthen drinking water infrastructure across the Commonwealth.

These investments will support critical testing, planning, and infrastructure improvements that help protect public health, improve water quality, and ensure safer, more reliable drinking water for families throughout the CNMI. 

We appreciate the continued federal partnership in addressing these long-term infrastructure needs and safeguarding our communities for future generations.

Our office is pleased to share that $1 million in Community Project Funding for the Commonwealth’s Department of Public Works has been included in the FY 2027 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development appropriations bill approved by the House Appropriations Subcommittee. 

The funding will support improvements to Route 317 (Gualo Rai Road), including roadway safety enhancements, improved accessibility, and drainage infrastructure upgrades to help reduce flooding and protect surrounding areas.

This investment represents an important step toward strengthening local infrastructure and improving public safety for our community. The bill will now advance to the full House Appropriations Committee for further consideration before moving to the House floor.

Our office was proud to support the advancement of several bipartisan bills through the House Small Business Committee that strengthen accountability, improve federal programs, and expand opportunities for small businesses. 

We look forward to continuing to work with our colleagues in Congress to help ensure these efforts deliver meaningful benefits to entrepreneurs, job creators, and communities across the CNMI and the nation.
